title: Console usage ingestion mesh: resilient schema healthcheck and lineage tracing
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Add a lightweight, horizontally-scalable schema healthcheck and event-lineage tracing component to the Console usage ingestion mesh. This ticket implements: (1) continuous schema assertions sampled from production traffic with adaptive sampling to keep cost predictable, (2) a lineage header that follows an event through the mesh (origin -> transformer -> validator -> sink) for faster root-cause and backfill planning, and (3) an automated canary replay and soft-coercion path for schema drift remediation. The service should be pluggable into existing intake gateways and emit health metrics and actionable alerts to the Console dashboards. Design constraints: minimal per-event overhead (<= 2ms added p95), backwards-compatible headers, and non-blocking mode by default with opt-in strict mode per-tenant.
acceptance_criteria: Healthcheck agent deployed behind the ingestion mesh that samples 1-5% of traffic and runs schema assertions with <5% false-positive rate
Events carry a lineage header (X-RW-Lineage) that is propagated end-to-end and can be resolved in Console trace UI
Canary replay harness that can replay sampled events into a strict validator without impacting production sinks
Soft-coercion layer implemented: when strict assertions fail, a configurable coercion rule set attempts best-effort normalization and emits a corrective metric
Telemetry: per-tenant schema-health score, drift-rate, top-violating-field list, and associated alerting configured in console-2026.03
Deployment load tests demonstrate added latency <= 2ms p95 at target sampling rates and CPU < 10% on gateway nodes for default config
tasks: Design schema-healthcheck agent API and sampling policy (proto + HTTP contract)
Add X-RW-Lineage header generation and propagation in gateway and transformers
Implement assertion engine with pluggable rule adapters (json-schema, typed-rules)
Build canary replay harness and playback sandbox in staging
Wire metrics to Console dashboards and add alerting playbooks
Create rollout plan: opt-in tenants -> canary hosts -> global gradual rollout
Author runbook and incident KB for schema drift and false positives
comments: 2026-03-02 - Aisha Patel: Kicked off design doc; initial prototype of assertion engine uses json-schema and a small typed-rule shim. Prototype shows ~1.2ms p95 overhead when sampling 2% of events.

2026-03-05 - Liam O'Connor: Spike result: memory overhead on gateway container increases 18MB with agent loaded as sidecar. Decision: start with in-process library behind feature flag for lower operational complexity.
2026-03-07 - Priya Desai (PM): Prioritized lineage header to speed up incident TTR. Ask: include tenant_id and ingest-shard as fields inside the header for correlation with billing data.
2026-03-09 - Ben Kim (SRE): Load test notes: with 5% sampling at peak traffic we see CPU increase ~6% and 0.9ms added median latency. Need to cap sampling per-tenant to avoid hotspots.

2026-03-11 - Liam O'Connor: Implemented canary replay harness in staging; discovered transformation ordering affects assertion results. Trade-off: run assertions post-transform by default to avoid schema churn from upstream enrichers.
2026-03-13 - Aisha Patel: Added soft-coercion rule set prototype and metrics; created initial alert thresholds: drift-rate > 0.5%/hour triggers paging for high-impact tenants.
2026-03-14 - Design review: approved with two follow-ups: (1) formalize rule-of-thumb for sampling budgets per tenant, (2) add GDPR-safe hashing for lineage header when PII may be present.
notes: Keep strict mode opt-in per-tenant to avoid accidental outages for legacy customers.
Lineage header should be compact (base62 token) and resolvable to a stored trace object; avoid sending full trace JSON in every request.
Soft-coercion rules will be configurable via Console UI in a later ticket; store default rules in central rule-registry service.
Evaluate integration with existing telemetry pipeline (telemetry-ingest) for historical drift analysis and backfills.
